artworks.title: American Scoter Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting depicts two American Scoter Ducks swimming in the water. One duck has dark plumage and an orange beak, while the other has grey-toned feathers and a more subdued beak. The ducks are shown gliding on the water's surface, with detailed patterns on their feathers and reflections in the water. The water has gentle waves, contributing to a sense of movement in the scene. The style of the painting is reminiscent of John James Audubon's detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Havell's Tern and Trudeau's Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This image shows a side view of two terns on a rocky outcrop overlooking a serene body of water. The horizon, distant landforms, and scattered buildings provide a backdrop. The terns are depicted with detailed brushstrokes capturing their feathers and patterns. The color palette includes blues, grays, whites, and warm earth tones. The sky transitions from pale blue to a soft blush near the horizon. Variegated seashells and stones are scattered around the terns.

artworks.title: Marsh Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Marsh Tern diving towards an insect. The image depicts a Marsh Tern in full descent with its wings extended and body pointed downward. The bird's plumage is detailed with varying shades of white and grey, and its head has a darker cap. The background is a soft blue color. To the lower left, there is a small depiction of an insect, which the bird seems to be targeting. The style is similar to John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Common American Swan
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a swan on a pond with yellow water lilies. The swan is depicted with detail in its plumage, with its long, curved neck forming an arch as it skims the water. The painting captures the scene with reflective water that mirrors the swan's shape. Surrounding the swan are yellow water lilies and green lily pads. The background includes trees and a pale blue sky.

artworks.title: Violet-green Cormorant and Townsend's Cormorant
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two cormorants on a rock. One cormorant is depicted with striking iridescent green feathers, sharp eyes, and a sleek silhouette, while the other has subtler brown plumage and a more robust stance. Both birds are illustrated with naturalistic detail, including their webbed feet and streamlined bodies. The background suggests the horizon over an ocean or large body of water, and the overall ambiance is calm and natural.

artworks.title: Californian Partridge
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Californian Partridges against a landscape background. The painting depicts two birds standing on a patch of earth, with one bird slightly crouched. The bird in the foreground displays intricate patterns on its feathers, with a mix of brown, blue, and other colors, while the bird behind it showcases similar features and coloring. The landscape in the background stretches out with rolling hills and a winding river, painted in earth tones and blues, creating a natural setting. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for his detailed portrayal of birds.

artworks.title: Golden-winged Warbler and Cape May Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a branch with four colorful birds perched on it. The painting depicts two species of warblers, identified as the Golden-winged Warbler and the Cape May Warbler. The Golden-winged Warblers have yellow patches on their wings and head and their bodies are rendered in shades of grey, blue, and white. The Cape May Warblers have a bright orange-red head and chest, lightly spotted, with a more yellow-brown color palette. The detailed foliage consists of slender branches with large, green leaves tinged with autumnal browns, showcasing the birds and their natural habitat. This painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Brown Creeper and Californian Nuthatch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a tree branch and one bird in flight. The artwork showcases two birds, one perched toward the top of a gnarled tree branch, while another clings upside down on the side. One bird is depicted in mid-flight, its wings spread wide displaying intricate patterns of brown and white feathers. The tree is portrayed with a rough bark texture and patches of lichen. Warm, natural hues emphasize the birds’ plumage and the details of the tree. This style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed illustrations of birds.

artworks.title: Hairy Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a group of woodpeckers perched on a barren tree. The painting features different woodpecker species depicted in detail, showcasing their plumage colors. The tree is without leaves, emphasizing the birds. The artwork presents the woodpeckers in natural poses that suggest interaction, in the style similar to John James Audubon's lifelike bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Maria's Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a tree with woodpeckers perched on its branches. The color palette includes blacks, whites, browns, and subtle shades of red and yellow on the birds. One woodpecker has a red accent on its head, and another is looking upwards. Other woodpeckers are scattered on the branches, some with their heads facing downwards and others facing forward. The background is off-white.

artworks.title: American Ptarmigan and White-tailed Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two birds standing on a rocky terrain with a distant mountainous background. One bird is resting with its head lowered, showing intricate patterns of white, brown, and black on its feathers. The other bird stands upright, displaying a primarily white body with gray details and red markings around its eye. The background showcases gradients of blue, suggesting a calm sky with overlapping silhouettes of mountains.

artworks.title: Little Tawny Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three birds are perched on the branches of a small tree with sparse green leaves and bright red berries. The topmost bird is brown with white and dark spots. The second bird is small with a uniform brown tone and slightly upturned tail. The largest bird at the bottom has dark plumage with light streaks on its wings. The birds have brown, black, and gray plumage, the leaves are green, and the berries are vivid red and orange. The birds are arranged vertically from top to bottom along the branch.

artworks.title: Prairie Starling
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds on budding branches. The painting depicts one bird with dark glossy plumage, a striking red shoulder patch, and a blue-black body sitting on the lower branch, while another bird with a lighter brownish body and faint stripes, perches above. The birds are positioned on slender branches with green buds. The overall composition highlights the contrast between the colors of the birds and the tones of the branches.

artworks.title: Brown Pelican
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a pelican standing on a rocky shore. The painting features a detailed depiction of a pelican, with its large beak open. The pelican is prominently placed in the foreground, showcasing its feather patterns and the textures between the bird's beak and feathers. In the background, a coastal landscape stretches into the distance, with calm waters, sandy shores, and a lighthouse against a blue sky with grey clouds. The color palette includes earthy tones for the bird and blues and greys for the seascape, creating a harmonious scene. This is in style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Rough-legged Falcon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two rough-legged falcons are perched on a tree branch. One bird has darker plumage and the other has a more reddish-brown coloring. The birds have yellow beaks and feet. The bird on the left is lower on the branch and has its beak open. The bird on the right is positioned above it and also has its beak open.

artworks.title: Plumed Partridge and Thick-legged Partridge
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three large birds with distinct plumage, prominently depicted in the foreground. The left bird has blue, brown, and white feathers with long black plumes on its head. The middle bird is bending its head towards the ground, showcasing similar colors. The bird on the right has mottled brown and cream-colored feathers and stands facing forward. The color palette is earthy with shades of brown, blue, and white against a light sky-blue background with mountain outlines. The scene captures the birds side by side on a grassy patch of land, with the center bird slightly bowing its head.

artworks.title: Lazuli Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Six birds are depicted on branches of a bare tree with budding leaves. The illustration's color palette consists of browns, yellows, pinks, and hints of blue against a neutral background. At the top sits a small brown and blue bird on the highest branch. Below, a bird with pink, brown, and white plumage perches. Further down, a bird with rich brown and pink colors is situated. To the bottom left, a bird with a yellow chest and black wings perches, and near the center, a bird with brown and black wings with a hint of yellow stands. In the lower right, a brown bird with a white speckled belly sits. The tree branches extend vertically through the center of the image, supporting the birds at varying heights.

artworks.title: Columbian Humming Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image showcases several hummingbirds interacting with and around a tall plant adorned with pink flowers. The color palette includes various shades of green, pink, and red, contrasted by neutral tones in the background and hummingbird bodies. The plant extends vertically through the center, with hummingbirds positioned around it, two hovering near the blossoms on the left and one perched near a nest at the base. Another hummingbird is perched on a branch to the right.

artworks.title: Californian Vulture
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a California vulture standing on a log. The painting features a California vulture standing on a log. The vulture has dark feathers, a red head and neck that transitions into shades of orange and blue, and detailed feathers. The vulture's talons grip the log. The background is plain.

artworks.title: White-Legged Oyster-Catcher and Slender-Billed Oyster-Catcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two oystercatchers on a rocky shoreline. The scene features a pair of birds: one with vivid red legs and a bright red beak, characterized by dark plumage and a striking orange eye. The other bird has one leg visible and a beak pointed downward, appearing to inspect or forage near shells on the rock surface. The background shows a gradual transition from earth tones of the rocks to soft blues of the sky and water.

artworks.title: Townsend's Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds in flight above a body of water. The birds are depicted a mid-flight, showcasing intricate details in their feathers and varying tones of grey, black, and white. The lower bird has darker plumage with distinct white markings on its wings and a sharp, pointed beak. The upper bird appears lighter in color with a combination of grey and white feathers and a slender, elongated body. The background is minimal with a soft gradient representing the sky and a subtle suggestion of the horizon line above the blue expanse of water.

artworks.title: Western Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two ducks near a body of water with grass reeds. The image features a pair of ducks standing on a riverbank or lakeside beside tall grasses. The foreground displays a duck bending its neck forward towards the water's edge, while the background shows another duck among the reeds. The depiction of the ducks is highly realistic, capturing the intricate details of their feathers and the calm natural setting.

artworks.title: Slender-billed Guillemot
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two Slender-billed Guillemots standing on a rocky cliff. The birds are perched on a greenish-brown rocky surface overlooking a vast expanse of blue sea under a sky filled with clouds. The bird on the left has dark brown plumage with light brown patterning on its body, while the bird on the right is black and white. The setting showcases a coastal environment.

artworks.title: American Flamingo
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A dark pink flamingo stands on a shallow outcropping, craning its neck down toward a pool of pale blue water in this vertical print. Shown in profile facing our left, the bird has a curving tan, orange, and black bill, and the eye we can see is bright blue. One charcoal-gray feather tucks under its wing, but the rest of the feathers and its legs are deep rose pink. One webbed foot steps forward, toward the edge of the low, rocky outcropping at the water’s edge. Muted green growth covers the ground, and the exposed edge of the rock is brown. Pale blue water extends back to the horizon, which comes about a third of the way up the composition. Eight pale pink and white flamingos, small in scale in the distance, walk or stand near sandbars in the placid waterway. The sky has a narrow band of light blue along the horizon, and the rest of the background is white. Across the top of the page, nine anatomical drawings, seeming to be lightly sketched, float against the white background. They are details of the bird’s beak, tongue, and foot. Each is numbered from one to nine. In the upper left corner of the paper, text reads, “No. 87.” and in the upper right, “Plate CCCCXXXI.” An inscription in the center margin below the printed image reads, “America Flamingo, PHOENICOPTERUS RUBERT, Linn. Old Male.” To the left is a numbered key: “1. Profile view of Bill at its greatest extension. 2. Superior front view of upper Mandible 3. Interior front view of upper Mandible. 4. Interior front view of lower Mandible. 5. Interior front view of lower Mandible with the Tongue in.” It continues to the right: “6. Profile view of Tongue. 7. Superior front view of Tongue. 8. Inferior front view of Tongue. 9. Perpendicular front view of the foot fully expanded.” Smaller text under the lower left corner of the printed image reads, “Drawn from Nature by J. J. Audubon, F.R.S. F.L.S.” And to the right: “Engraved. Printed and Coloured by Rob. Havell. 1838.”
